newsitem.title: USA: Striking L.A. harbor pilots ordered not to picket.
newsitem.headline: Striking L.A. harbor pilots ordered not to picket.

text.p: Striking maritime pilots were ordered on Tuesday to end their picketing at the Port of Los Angeles, the West Coast's busiest harbour, which is snarled by a shipping logjam.
But Long Beach Superior Court Commissioner Anita Rae Shapiro did not order the pilots back to work, as the city of Los Angeles had requested.
Shapiro ordered the 14 pilots to stop picketing at the port, where some 1,500 dock workers had refused to cross the picket lines.
As a result, ships have not been loaded or unloaded for four days, causing a traffic jam.
Port spokeswoman Barbara Yamamoto said 11 ships were at berth Tuesday, with eight more anchored outside the harbour and 20 more scheduled to arrive by Friday.
She said two managers who are qualified pilots would guide vessels in and out of berths in an effort to break the logjam.
The city of Los Angeles went to court on Tuesday to order the striking pilots back to work. City spokesman Keith Comrie accused the strikers of not negotiating in good faith.
But in her ruling, Shapiro only told the pilots not to picket at the terminal or at the harbour department's offices.
The temporary order expires on July 24, when a new hearing will be held.
The pilots were seeking a 72 percent pay raise from $113,712 to $195,000 over two years to bring them in line, they say, with pilots in other U.S. ports.
The city has offered a four-year package amounting to a 17 percent raise to $133,000 in salary plus overtime and other benefits, including a retirement plan.
